ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), including Part 8A on Registers of Significant Beneficial Owners inserted by the Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2021; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Sanctions Act 1979; Russia Sanctions Act 2022; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 for FMC reporting entity aspects; Trusts Act 2019 for trust-origin UBO structures; and FATF Recommendations as implemented by the New Zealand AML/CFT supervision framework

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the biometric passport page of each Significant Beneficial Owner / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or authorized statutory document examiner in the UBO's country of residence or nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin; or Consular Legalization by the nearest New Zealand Embassy or High Commission if the country is not an Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or government-issued ID showing current address) for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated bank, or issuing government authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required for acceptance by the New Zealand Companies Office and AML/CFT reporting entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or Certificate of Good Standing of the immediate corporate shareholder / parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the parent entity's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of Directors and Shareholders or official UBO register extract of the corporate shareholder / parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or statutory registered agent of the corporate shareholder / parent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution authorizing the incorporation, name adoption, and appointment of the New Zealand resident director and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the beneficial parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for initial capital and incorporation expenses
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of the UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization with notarial certification of the signatory

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media, PEP, and financial sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors, corporate shareholders, and project counterparties against: (i) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) watchlists and the New Zealand Sanctions Register; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury (UK) Consolidated List; (v) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (vi) New Zealand domestic designation instruments under the Sanctions Act 1979 and Russia Sanctions Act 2022. Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, with senior-management approval of the relationship documentation under FATF Recommendations 12, 13, and 14 and the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal operated by the New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies Office naming guidelines, a proposed company name must be expressed in English or te reo Māori using Latin-alphabet characters, numerals, and limited punctuation; non-English names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must include the suffix 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Tāpui', or 'Tapui' (or stated full form) and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name on the New Zealand register, must not be offensive, must not imply a connection with the Crown, a government department, or a local authority, and must not mislead contrary to the Fair Trading Act 1986.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The statutory name reservation runs for 20 working days (approximately 28 calendar days). Within 20 working days of a name-rejection notice issued under s 22 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may: (1) request detailed written reasons from the Companies Office; (2) file a 'Name Reservation Review Request' with the Registrar of Companies, including any letters of consent or trademark evidence; (3) submit an amended name through the Companies Register portal for expedited re-screening; and (4) if the refusal is maintained, seek judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. A rejected name may be resubmitted after the expiry of the applicable 20-working-day review period and upon payment of the prescribed name-reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A virtual office in New Zealand is accepted for Companies Act compliance only where a genuine physical address is operated in New Zealand by a licensed corporate services provider, registered agent, law firm, or chartered accountant that accepts service of legal process during ordinary business hours. However, for an OOG heavy industrial project cargo logistics company, the entity must also demonstrate economic substance: a New Zealand resident director, local banking arrangements, books and records maintained in New Zealand, and decision-making documentation evidencing operational control of project-cargo contracts; a pure virtual office without operational records will materially increase audit and transfer-pricing exposure under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the OECD BEPS framework.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 5–8% per annum for a non-licensed, low-risk logistics entity; the probability rises to 15–20% if unannounced inspections are triggered by adverse UBO filings, customs clearances of out-of-gauge cargo, suspicious transaction reports, or inconsistencies between the virtual office and the declared logistics activities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), in particular sections 12–14 (registration of company), 16 (constitution), 18 (certificate of incorporation), 28 (default constitution), 30–33 (registered office), 42–56 (share capital and share issues), 110–131 (directors and board powers, including s 122 exercise of powers), 157 (director residence requirement), 189–202 (shareholders' meetings); Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994; Financial Reporting Act 2013 (exemptions for certain overseas-owned small companies where applicable).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ngā Kōtui Kōmihana o Aotearoa), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Office online incorporation application, e-filing portal 'Register a company', corresponding to Form CO/01), together with the required statutory consents and registered office declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Companies Act 1993; shares may be fully or partly paid and consideration must satisfy the solvency and fair-value rules in sections 52–56 of the Act. No escrow account or capital deposit is mandated by the Companies Office; the board must, however, record the subscription consideration in the share allotment records and file accurate shareholder particulars on incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company') — RESOLVED, unanimously, that: (1) the incorporation of the Company by the New Zealand Companies Office and the adoption of its constitution be and are hereby ratified and confirmed; (2) the initial share capital of the Company be and is hereby subscribed and allotted as set out in the allotment schedule annexed, with the receipt of aggregate subscription consideration of NZ$[amount] being acknowledged and recorded as fully paid share capital; (3) the directors, having made due inquiry, confirm that the Company is solvent immediately after the allotment and that the consideration satisfies sections 52–56 of the Companies Act 1993; (4) the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [address], New Zealand, and the Company Secretary is directed to notify the Registrar of any change of registered office in accordance with section 31 of the Companies Act 1993; (5) [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Company Secretary, each with authority to execute contracts, open and operate bank accounts, and file statutory documents, subject to section 122 of the Companies Act 1993; (6) [Bank] be and is hereby designated as the principal banker of the Company and the officers are authorised to complete account mandates and banking forms; and (7) the officers be and are hereby authorised to do all acts and execute all instruments necessary to give full effect to these resolutions. Dated this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register online search portal (https://register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a real-time name availability search on the Companies Register. Verify the proposed name against existing registered companies and against prohibited or restricted words under the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994. If the name is available and the applicant wishes to secure it, submit an online name reservation application; the Registrar will hold a reserved name for up to 28 days pending lodgement of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of the applicant
Statement of business purpose corresponding to ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510
Letters of consent for any restricted words (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name as confusingly similar or objectionable, the applicant may submit written submissions, obtain a letter of consent from the holder of the similar name, or adopt a modified name and re-file the reservation; a refusal notice may be reviewed by the Registrar upon written application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitutional Documents and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company counsel and proposed directors (pre-lodgement internal step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution (or elect to rely on the default constitution in section 28 of the Companies Act 1993), prepare each director's consent to act, obtain a written consent from the owner of the registered office address, and execute shareholder subscription documents. Where the company is the CK_IC International Company classification, ensure the constitution does not restrict the company's object to New Zealand domestic activities and authorises cross-border project cargo contracts, out-of-gauge heavy-haul operations, and settlement via milestone wire transfers and documentary letters of credit. All documents must be dated and signed before the application is lodged.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Companies Office prescribed form) for each director
Consent to use of registered office address
Shareholder subscription letters and shareholder resolution
Address for service in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a consent or constitution is rejected for defective execution, re-execute the instrument before a notary public or Justice of the Peace, correct the company's legal name, and re-submit to the Companies Office prior to incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online incorporation filing via the 'Register a company' portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Application for Registration of a Company (CO/01). Input the company name, registered office address, constitution status, names and residential addresses of directors and shareholders, and the number of shares to be held by each shareholder. Attach the scanned consents. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZ$105.45 (approximately USD 65) by credit or debit card. Ensure at least one director is resident in New Zealand or in a jurisdiction with an enforcement arrangement in force with New Zealand (currently Australia) as required by section 157 of the Companies Act 1993. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval, at which time the company comes into existence.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query pursuant to sections 12–14 of the Companies Act 1993, respond in writing within 15 working days, amend the application particulars, or withdraw and refile. A final refusal may be appealed to the High Court of New Zealand by way of judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NZBN, Inland Revenue and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake) and the NZBN Registry administered by MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the company is automatically allocated a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Access Inland Revenue's myIR portal to register the company for income tax and obtain an IRD number; complete an IR596 application where manual registration is needed. Determine mandatory registration obligations: GST registration where taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period; PAYE and KiwiSaver employer registration if employees are engaged; and applicable non-resident withholding tax or treaty relief obligations in relation to milestone wire payments and letter-of-credit settlements. Provide non-resident shareholding details and the relevant double tax agreement residence position if beneficial owners are treaty-resident outside New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Directors' and shareholders' identification (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 verification)
Non-resident certificate of residence for treaty relief
Project cargo contract summaries to evidence taxable activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where Inland Revenue rejects or delays the registration due to entity verification failure, re-submit certified director identification, use the myIR document upload facility to transmit the Certificate of Incorporation, and escalate to the Inland Revenue Business Registration service with a request for expedited manual review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Officer Appointment and Bank Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; a registered New Zealand trading bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or pass the First Board Resolution by circular written resolution signed by all directors). Adopt the First Board Resolution approving share subscriptions, fixing the registered office, and appointing the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary. Issue share certificates and update the share register. Open a corporate operating account with a New Zealand bank, providing the certified incorporation certificate, constitution, First Board Resolution, and passport evidence of signatories to satisfy customer due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. The account should be structured to support milestone wire transfers and documentary letter-of-credit operations for OOG project cargo settlement.
required_dossiers: Director identification documents and proof of residential address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence for the CK_IC International Company structure, provide an organisational chart, a certificate of good standing, an apostilled copy of the incorporation certificate under the Hague Apostille Convention, and a board resolution confirming the source of funds; refile any corrected documents within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Compliance and Operational Licensing Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; WorkSafe New Zealand; Waka Kotahi NZ Transport Agency; Territorial Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company's first annual return with the Companies Office within twelve months of incorporation and thereafter annually, paying the applicable annual return fee. Maintain statutory registers (share register, director register, charges register and accounting records) at the registered office. Before commencing physical OOG heavy-haul movements, verify whether an Overdimension/Overweight permit is required from Waka Kotahi for each route; if the company operates a cargo depot or staging yard, obtain a Resource Consent for land use from the territorial authority and a Building Warrant of Fitness/Fire Safety Certificate under the Building Act 2004, and notify WorkSafe New Zealand of any hazardous substances on site pursuant to the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.
required_dossiers: Statutory registers and accounting records address
Resource consent or permitted activity certificate for depot
Building warrant of fitness and fire safety certificate
Insurance certificates for heavy-haul cargo and public liability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company is placed on the removal register for failure to file an annual return, apply for reinstatement under section 328 of the Companies Act 1993 on payment of the prescribed reinstatement fee and outstanding filings. If a transport permit is refused, appeal to Waka Kotahi with a revised route engineering assessment, axle-load calculations and a police escort plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (occupational health and safety); Waka Kotahi New Zealand Transport Agency (overdimension/overweight movement permits); Territorial Authorities and regional councils under the Resource Management Act 1991 (land use and environmental effects); Environmental Protection Authority (national environmental standards).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated statutory Manufacturing/Industrial Operating Licence is imposed on ISIC 5229 freight arrangement and project cargo logistics services in New Zealand. Where the entity performs physical heavy-haul staging, it must hold an Overdimension/Overweight Vehicle Permit issued by Waka Kotahi for each route, a Resource Consent (or permitted activity certificate) for any fixed cargo yard or depot, and a Building Warrant of Fitness/Fire Safety Certificate for any occupied premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand, with regional councils and territorial authorities exercising delegated functions under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Permitted/Controlled Activity - Registration-level screening under the Resource Management Act 1991; a full Environmental Impact Assessment will only be triggered for project cargo operations involving land reclamation, significant earthworks, expansion of coastal infrastructure, or storage/disposal of hazardous substances above specified thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) for diesel particulate matter, NOx and PM10/PM2.5 emission limits from heavy-haul vehicles and generators; National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water; Hazardous Substances (Storage) Regulations 2017 for class and quantity notification; trade waste discharge approval from the local council for depot washdown water and stormwater management; no environmental discharge is generated by the banking and settlement component (milestone wire and letter-of-credit operations).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Building Act 2004 - Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF), fire safety systems certification and regular inspection by the territorial authority; structural load assessment of floors and racking systems to NZS 1170.5 and NZS 1170.2 for storage of out-of-gauge cargo; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 - workplace risk assessment, hazardous substances notification to WorkSafe, emergency response planning with Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), and occupational exposure monitoring for noise and airborne particulates during heavy-haul operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand (Te Tari Taake); secure taxpayer portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz. For export customs clearance, the competent adjunct authority is the New Zealand Customs Service (TRADEX / Trade Single Window) under the Customs and Excise Act 2018.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Confirm non-resident status of the CK_IC International Company (not incorporated in NZ; central management and control exercised offshore; no NZ permanent establishment). Step 2: If the entity derives NZ-sourced income or carries on a taxable activity in NZ, apply to the IRD for an IRD number (unique tax file number used for both income tax and GST) using Form IR742 (Application for IRD number for non-resident individual/company), accompanied by certified constitutional documents (certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, register of directors/shareholders, bank reference) for AML/CFT due diligence. Step 3: If the company is registered on the NZ Companies Register as an overseas company, first obtain an NZBN (New Zealand Business Number) from the Companies Office (Companies Act 1993) and quote it in the IR742. Step 4: Apply for GST registration in the same IR742 or via myIR, electing voluntary registration (GST Act 1985 s 51(3)) where turnover is below NZD 60,000, or compulsory registration if taxable supplies exceed the threshold; appoint a New Zealand GST agent and provide a NZ address for service if no physical presence exists. Step 5: The IRD will issue the GST registration number (same numeric as the IRD number) and the entity will file periodic GST returns (GST101) online. No separate VAT ID ledger exists in NZ.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the CK_IC offshore International Company is classified as a non-resident foreign company outside the NZ corporate income tax base. NZ applies a source-based income tax to foreign-registered entities: all foreign-source project cargo freight, demurrage, deviation, and heavy-haul international logistics income derived offshore is exempt from NZ income tax, provided no NZ P.E. exists, no director meetings/management are held in NZ, and no NZ-source income is derived. Any NZ-domestic standard-rated GST activities (e.g., inland haul to port) are within the indirect tax net. Had the entity been NZ-resident, Entity_Level_Taxation at 28% with imputation credits would apply; the stated Tax_Exempt_Zone classification therefore requires strict substance documentation of offshore management and control.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification. Available statutory elections: (i) voluntary GST registration election (GST Act 1985 s 51(3)) below the NZD 60,000 threshold, enabling input refund recovery for non-residents with a taxable activity; (ii) GST return basis election — cash (payments) basis vs invoice basis (s 19, generally mandatory > NZD 2 million turnover); (iii) GST group registration election (s 55) for affiliated NZ entities to file a single consolidated GST return; (iv) export zero-rating election under s 11 for goods exported within 28 days and for offshore services to non-residents; (v) Look-Through Company election (Income Tax Act 2007 subpart HA) — only for NZ-resident closely held companies (max 5 shareholders) converting entity-level taxation to pass-through treatment; (vi) no hybrid mismatch election is generally available — NZ's hybrid mismatch integrity rules (subpart FH) instead deny deductions or impose inclusions automatically for cross-border dual-inclusion structures; structural changes creating hybrid entities must be disclosed to the IRD. The CK_IC, as a non-resident offshore trader, may most relevantly exercise the voluntary GST registration election and the s 11 export zero-rating positions; it cannot elect LTC treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST — New Zealand Goods and Services Tax, a broad-based value-added tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by the Inland Revenue Department; exports are zero-rated and domestic supplies are taxable at 15%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (New Zealand dollars) of total taxable supplies in any 12-month period, including projected/turnover from intended activity, if the non-resident carries on a taxable activity in NZ. Registration is compulsory at or above this threshold; the non-resident may voluntarily register below it to recover input GST. No sub-national (state/city) sales tax threshold applies — NZ is a unitary national GST system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no statutory pre-clearance API obligation for invoices in NZ. E-invoicing is voluntary and implemented via the Peppol network (NZ e-Invoicing interoperability standard); IRD accepts electronic invoices if authenticity and integrity are maintained, and records must be retained for 7 years. GST returns (GST101) are filed electronically through myIR or IRD-enabled accounting software; customs outward declarations are cleared through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (TRADEX), while Inland Revenue receives export data by data exchange. For high-value OOG project export cargo, the exporter should also transmit the advance export/cargo manifest (ACH / Customs export entry) prior to vessel departure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% GST) for the CK_IC project cargo logistics business requires satisfaction of GST Act 1985 s 11 criteria: (i) goods — supply of goods exported from NZ by the supplier (or delivered as ship's stores) with physical export within 28 days of the time of supply, proven by a Customs Export Declaration and bill of lading/air waybill evidencing final destination outside NZ; (ii) services — supply to a non-resident customer at a location outside NZ at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not directly connected with NZ real property or moveable personal property, and are not received by the non-resident while in NZ in connection with a taxable activity carried on here; (iii) international transport — freight, charter, stevedoring, and handling services for the offshore leg of OOG/heavy-haul cargo movement to or from NZ are zero-rated as international transport; the NZ-domestic leg (depot/quay to the NZ port threshold) is standard-rated unless it forms part of an export through-transport contract and is separately disclosed as zero-rated international carriage. The exporter must retain the outward Customs Export Declaration, the bill of lading/waybill, commercial/project contract, foreign-currency or NZD settlement evidence, and a Letter of Credit/inward remittance certificate to demonstrate that the recipient is non-resident and consideration is attributable to the exported goods or offshore services; voluntary or compulsory GST registration is required to support the refund claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service electronic outward entry via TRADEX/Trade Single Window, with OOG cargo manifest) — statutory evidence of physical export.
Bill of Lading (ocean/breakbulk or multimodal through bill for out-of-gauge heavy lift cargo, issued to the non-resident project owner) or Air Waybill where airfreight is used.

Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign-currency settlement proof, or Letter of Credit documentary drawing evidence) — accepted by IRD audit as substantiating the export sale and the 180-day FX repatriation milestone.
Commercial invoice, project logistics services agreement and packing/flat-rack or breakbulk survey report evidencing the OOG scope and the non-resident counter-party.
Shipping/transport movement records (vessel stowage plan, sailing sheet, rail haul manifest) evidencing export within the 28-day statutory window.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD audit verification of zero-rating and GST refund claims for non-resident exporters focuses on: physical export within the 28-day statutory window; genuineness and offshore location of the foreign recipient; absence of NZ-domestic service components; and, in bank-documented project cargo contracts, correspondence between the contract payment milestones (wire/Letter of Credit), inward remittance, and the declared consideration. Where goods are not exported within 28 days, the supply ceases to be zero-rated and the full consideration becomes standard-rated 15% output tax, assessed retrospectively with use-of-money interest. Incorrect/inflated refund claims expose the CK_IC to Tax Administration Act 1994 civil penalties and retrospective clawback: not taking reasonable care 20%; unacceptable tax position 20%; gross carelessness 40%; abusive tax position 100%; evasion 150% of the shortfall; plus late payment and use-of-money interest (underpayment rate approximately 10.7% per annum, adjusted quarterly). Criminal prosecution applies to fraudulent zero-rating or knowingly false export documentation — first offence fines up to NZD 50,000 and subsequent offences up to NZD 100,000 (and equivalent imprisonment for individuals), with director/agent personal liability in cases of aiding, abetting, or false GST refund applications. IRD assessment periods: generally four years (Tax Administration Act 1994 s 108), but no time bar for evasion or fraudulent/wilfully misleading returns, enabling an unlimited retrospective clawback. Additionally, the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007 s BG 1 / GA 1) may reconstruct the arrangement if the zero-rated offshore structure or the 180-day FX deferral is used to create GST timing or income-tax advantages without commercial substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) pursuant to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, operating in coordination with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) for AML/CFT supervision, and with the Toitū Te Whenua Overseas Investment Office for inbound foreign investment screening. New Zealand has no discrete statutory foreign exchange control regulator; the RBNZ exercises prudential oversight, monetary policy, and payment system settlement through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a fully freely convertible G10 currency. Exchange controls were abolished in 1984, and neither the current account nor the capital account is subject to registration, licensing, quantitative limits, or prior approval for non-residents. Profit remittance from an International Company (IC) holding a New Zealand bank account is unrestricted: dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, and loan redemptions may be wired abroad without any exchange control consent, subject only to statutory tax withholding (Non-Resident Withholding Tax on interest and dividends, Approved Issuer Levy on eligible debt securities, and the thin-capitalisation rules in Part 4F of the Income Tax Act 2007). The only practical constraints are: (a) the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which requires consent for acquisitions of significant business assets (value threshold approximately NZD 100 million) or of sensitive land; (b) CRS/AEOI due diligence reporting by the New Zealand bank; and (c) AML/CFT source-of-funds verification performed by New Zealand reporting entities. For a project-cargo and heavy-haul logistics entity, no Overseas Investment Office consent is triggered by an ordinary equity injection or working capital advance, and the entity may freely hold NZD, USD, EUR, and other currencies and switch treasury positions without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender or conversion rules exist in New Zealand law. There is no statutory timeline for repatriating export receipts and no mandatory conversion ratio into NZD. An Out-of-Gauge heavy industrial project cargo logistics provider may retain all offshore invoice settlement balances in the currencies received, may hold foreign currency accounts indefinitely, and may deploy funds externally without restriction. The only mandatory obligations are statistical in nature: exporters must respond to RBNZ balance-of-payments surveys when formally selected, and the IRD transfer pricing rules (Sections GC 6 to GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007) require arm's-length pricing on related-party cross-border receivables. None of these obligations require surrender, conversion, or repatriation of export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for initial equity subscription and multi-currency Operational Account (NZD/USD/EUR)
Operational Account with dedicated Trade and Working Capital and FX Online platforms; eligible for commercial letter-of-credit negotiation
Operational Account (multi-currency) with trade finance facilities for documentary import letters of credit, standby letters of credit, and performance guarantees
Operational Account for NZD domestic settlement via BECS/ESAS with limited cross-border trade nuance
Operational Account (domestic NZD focused; limited appetite for non-resident-owned offshore structures)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as an ancillary conduit; Low as a primary settlement bank. New Zealand law has no dedicated electronic money institution (EMI) licensing category. Offshore digital multi-currency platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Wise Platform, ClearJunction, Currencycloud) may lawfully serve the International Company only if they: (a) are registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; (b) maintain an AML/CFT compliance programme supervised by a New Zealand supervisor; and (c) route all NZD settlement through a licensed New Zealand bank because they are not members of the RBNZ's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). For an OOG project-cargo treasury, an offshore EMI can efficiently hold multi-currency master accounts and execute supplier payments in less-liquid corridors; however, the statutory protection of funds, insolvency recourse, and NZD clearing finality are materially inferior to a tier-1 New Zealand bank. The recommended architecture is a tier-1 New Zealand bank for NZD/ESAS final settlement, letter-of-credit issuance, and escrow, supplemented by one regulated EMI for foreign-currency pass-through in non-NZD supplier corridors, with all balances swept nightly back to the New Zealand bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The AML/CFT Act 2009 does not impose a strict statutory mandate for physical board appearance, but New Zealand bank risk appetite (shaped by the RBNZ/FMA AML/CFT supervision framework) requires, for a non-resident-owned International Company, either: (a) a face-to-face interview conducted at a New Zealand branch by the account manager with at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner; or (b) a fully remote enhanced digital onboarding path comprising a live video interview with the signing director and UBO, notarised or New Zealand-lawyer-certified passports, a New Zealand registered office address, and a qualifying introducer relationship (a New Zealand-licensed law or accounting firm under the bank's introducer programme) that certifies identity and source of funds. The Capital Escrow Account generally triggers the highest assurance level: the subscribing director may be required to appear physically before the bank or before a New Zealand consular officer or Notary Public (for example in Hong Kong or Singapore) to execute the escrow and security documents. A physical meeting of the full board is not required; remote board approval via written resolution executed electronically and certified by the New Zealand company secretary is standard practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity attributable to an offshore trust or layered corporate chain (including the IC's trust-protective structure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation; New Zealand Companies Office company extract identifying the entity; full register of members and ultimate beneficial owners; the controlling trust deed, trustee declarations, and protector consent; a corporate-structure chart annotated with percentage holdings; UBO identity documents (passport and proof of residential address); and a third-party sanctions and PEP screening report (e.g., Dow Jones or World-Check) confirming clean results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for the initial equity capital deposit into the Capital Escrow Account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executive board resolution authorising the subscription and designating the escrow; share subscription/allotment agreement; audited or independently reviewed financial statements of the contributor; 12 months of original bank statements evidencing legitimate accumulation; supporting commercial documentation (sale-and-purchase deeds, dividend vouchers, or draws from a regulated trust); and a signed source-of-wealth affidavit in the bank's prescribed form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound milestone wires to high-risk project-cargo corridors (e.g., Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, or Middle East subcontractors) that do not match the original invoice profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed project master agreement and milestone schedule; signed work-certification documents from the end client; subcontractor and supplier KYB files (certificates of incorporation, ownership structure, sanctions screening); pro-forma invoices and purchase orders matched to each milestone; bills of lading, air waybills, CMR notes, and gate-pass evidence; Incoterms transport documentation; and insurance certificates covering the heavy-haul movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party instructing or payee routing where the IC directs payment to a party not named in the underlying invoice
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual direct-payment or assignment clause; tripartite novation or payment-direction agreement signed by the end client, the IC, and the receiving counterparty; invoice reassignment notice; board resolution ratifying the treasury instruction; and a bank-recommended indemnity or declaration executed by the beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency ambiguity or tax-exempt-zone classification triggering tax-evasion suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: New Zealand Inland Revenue tax-residence certificate; IRD number registration confirmation; economic-substance memorandum documenting central management and control in New Zealand; board meeting minutes; payroll and staff presence evidence; a conclusive double-tax-agreement tie-breaker analysis by New Zealand tax counsel where dual residency is asserted; and CRS self-certification forms (Form 15 for entities).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political Exposed Person (PEP) listing or sanctions-name coincidence with a sanctioned vessel owner, logistics operator, or beneficial-owner namesake
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised explanation letter; full corporate CV of each director and UBO; professional licences and industry memberships; negative-media dossier compiled from a reputable screening vendor; a written legal opinion from New Zealand-licensed external counsel confirming the absence of any actual nexus to the sanctioned person; and confirmatory identification documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the inward equity or funding wire: the contributor's bank initiates a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank covering) to the New Zealand bank's correspondent account (typically a New York or Singapore correspondent for USD, and a London or EU correspondent for EUR), which then credits the beneficiary International Company account in Wellington or Auckland in NZD via the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). The credit instruction must reference the share-allotment resolution number and the Companies Office filing; the recommended ISO 20022 purpose code is EQUI (equity-related capital) with the remittance information field carrying the phrase 'Capital Contribution - Share Subscription per Board Resolution [date]'. For NZD amounts above the large-value threshold, the bank executes via ESAS wholesale high-value settlement; for sub-threshold amounts, the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) is used. The verification package must include: the original MT103; the SWIFT payment confirmation; the share register updated within 20 working days under Section 86 of the Companies Act 1993; the Return of Allotment (CSR) filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days; the allotment board resolution; an IRD Non-Resident Withholding Tax declaration confirming the contribution is equity rather than debt; and, where relevant, confirmation from the Toitū Te Whenua Overseas Investment Office that consent is not required because the transaction is an ordinary trading-company equity injection below the NZD 100 million significant-business-assets threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements execute across the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for milestone and vendor wires, cleared through the New Zealand bank's CHIPS/Fedwire or TARGET2 membership; (2) commercial documentary Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) for imported heavy-haul equipment (SPMT axle lines, mobile cranes, rigging gear) and for pre-shipment financing of out-of-gauge modules; (3) standby Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT760) and performance bank guarantees for the project bid and performance milestone obligations; and (4) domestic NZD payments to New Zealand subcontractors, port authorities, and rail operators via the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) for standard wires or the wholesale ESAS high-value stream where urgency and amount demand. Billing and reconciliation are denominated in the contract currency (usually USD or EUR), and the treasury uses a nightly sweep to concentrate balances into the Operational Account. Each outbound wire must carry a precise invoice and milestone reference together with Incoterms shipment evidence (bill of lading, air waybill, CMR) to survive audit review. The bank's Trade and Working Capital desk maintains, in parallel, the letter-of-credit register, discounting schedules, and freight-forwarding documentation in escrow.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (vanilla deliverables) in NZD/USD and NZD/EUR for tenors up to 24 months, customised to project milestone dates and documented under a New Zealand bank FX Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - expressly permitted for hedging the IC's USD flows against less-liquid currencies of the project-cargo corridors (IDR, VND, THB, KZT, INR) where offshore deliverability is unavailable; New Zealand banks transact these under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with a Credit Support Annex

Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD, EUR/USD) - permitted for matching the funding currency of the IC's capital and trade-finance facility against the revenue currency; requires ISDA 2002 master documentation with a standard credit support annex

European-style FX options - permitted for hedging contingent or tendered milestone cash flows; premiums paid upfront with a bilateral ISDA early-termination agreement; exotic barrier instruments are not permitted without prior treasury-committee resolution
FX swaps (swap deposits, spot-next/forward-next) - permitted for rolling short-term NZD/USD liquidity positions on the same ESAS settlement date without altering the underlying hedge book

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: NZ Registrar of Companies (NZ Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month after the annual return date, which is each anniversary of the company's incorporation; the Registrar issues an electronic reminder one month before the return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs escalating late-filing penalties; persistent default for 6 months or more triggers deregistration (administrative strike-off). Directors may be disqualified and held personally liable for company debts incurred during the period of default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Audit Report (Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: NZ Companies Office (for registered large/overseas entities); shareholders of record for exempt small companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be presented to shareholders within 5 months of the balance date and, if required to be filed, lodged with the Companies Office within 20 working days of presentation, effectively within 6 months of the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or file financial statements is an offence: fines up to NZD 10,000 per director per contravention; a court order may compel filing, and continued non-compliance can trigger Companies Office investigation and removal from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4) and Financial Summary (IR10)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due 7 July if filed electronically (or 15 July for paper); companies represented by a tax agent with an approved extension may file by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to NZD 500 apply, along with late payment interest on tax owed (currently 9.6% per annum); deliberate non-filing may result in prosecution and additional evasion penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 if the entity is a 'large company' (total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, annual revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees), is an FMC reporting entity, or is an overseas/international company not eligible for the small-company exemption. Shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting rights may also require an audit, and a tax-exempt international company deriving no New Zealand-sourced income must still file an annual return to evidence its exempt status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 reporting entities; Tier 2 entities may apply NZ IFRS with reduced disclosure (NZ IFRS RDR). The tax-exempt international company is taxed under the Income Tax Act 2007, with offshore income exempt and no New Zealand GST obligation if no New Zealand-sourced supplies are made.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no public UBO annual filing for ordinary international companies; the annual return filed with the Companies Office confirms all registered shareholders as at the return date. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members within 30 days, and the board must approve the transfer instrument. For AML/CFT purposes, the entity must maintain beneficial-ownership records under the AML/CFT Act 2009, but no separate UBO confirmation is submitted to the Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share Transfer Register and Instrument Files

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900–2,800 per annum for a New Zealand registered office, resident agent, and corporate secretarial administration for a non-resident international company
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–20,000 per annum for a stand-alone New Zealand statutory audit of a project-cargo logistics entity; waived (USD 0) if the unanimous-shareholder small-company audit exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% – New Zealand standard corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday applies to project cargo or heavy-haul logistics activities in New Zealand. A qualifying non-resident International Company classified under the Tax_Exempt_Zone model, deriving exclusively foreign-source income and carrying on no business through a New Zealand permanent establishment, bears a 0% effective New Zealand tax rate on that foreign income. New Zealand-source project-cargo income, however, is assessable at 28% on a branch-equivalent basis. The R&D tax credit (15%) is not available to logistics service providers unless qualifying experimental development is undertaken.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory year cap: New Zealand tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test or, failing that, the business continuity test (ITA 2007 ss IA 4–IA 7).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) – electronic lodgement through Inland Revenue's myIR secure online filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return (IR4) after the company's balance date; provisional tax is payable in three instalments during the income year; separate GST returns apply if the entity is GST-registered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard balance date of 31 March: the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following year-end. Companies using an approved tax agent may obtain an extension of time to file by 31 March of the following income year. Standard provisional tax instalment dates for a 31 March balancer are 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income under ordinary concepts less statutory exclusions: OOG project-cargo freight revenue, heavy-haul mobilization fees, demurrage, detention, standby charges and ancillary logistics income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Return only income having a New Zealand source under s YD 4 ITA 2007. Foreign-source income from overseas haulage legs is excluded for a non-resident International Company lacking a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in deriving assessable income under s DA 1: fuel, sub-contractor heavy-haul costs, route permits, pilot/escort vehicles, port charges, insurance, depreciation and allocable head-office overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions attributable to New Zealand-source income. Global overheads must be apportioned on a reasonable and consistent basis reflecting actual New Zealand activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Net Taxable Income or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equals Box 1 less Box 2. A negative figure produces a tax loss to be carried forward, subject to continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only New Zealand-source losses are available for carry-forward; foreign losses are not deductible against New Zealand-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Income Tax Payable or Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income multiplied by 28%, less imputation credits, resident withholding tax credits and provisional tax paid; refunds arise where credits exceed tax assessed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 28% branch-equivalent rate applies to New Zealand-source profits. Imputation credits are unavailable unless the International Company participates in the New Zealand imputation group. Profits repatriated to a foreign head office are subject to non-resident withholding tax separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses applied against current-year taxable income, supported by shareholder continuity schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a shareholder continuity schedule evidencing at least 49% continuity of beneficial ownership where the loss-offset claim relies on that test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$50 per month or part-month up to a maximum of NZ$500 for an IR4 return. Late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax immediately upon the due date, plus a further 1% per month thereafter. Use-of-money interest (UOMI) accrues at the IRD underpayment rate. Civil shortfall penalties may reach 100% of the tax shortfall for evasion. Criminal conviction under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143A can result in fines up to NZ$50,000 for an individual and NZ$100,000 for a body corporate, and imprisonment of up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% – statutory New Zealand non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid to non-residents. Resident withholding tax (RWT) on dividends to New Zealand-resident shareholders is 33%, with a 28% corporate rate for inter-company distributions. Under most New Zealand double tax agreements, the treaty dividend rate is 15% for portfolio holdings and 5% for substantial shareholdings (typically 10% or more, varying by treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) confirm the payee is the beneficial owner and a resident of the treaty jurisdiction; (2) obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the revenue authority of the residence country; (3) provide the TRC and a completed New Zealand DTA claim form to the New Zealand payer before the withholding event; (4) apply the reduced treaty rate at source; (5) if tax is over-withheld, file a refund claim with Inland Revenue within the four-year time bar under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 108; (6) retain the TRC, underlying contract and beneficial-ownership analysis for the statutory six-year record-keeping period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT rate is 15%; most New Zealand DTAs reduce the rate to 10%, and certain treaties allow 5% for industrial/commercial royalties. Interest: statutory NRWT rate is 15%; an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may replace NRWT on qualifying interest paid to non-residents; DTA rates on interest are commonly 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$10 million – the threshold at which Inland Revenue expects contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (Local File / Master File equivalent) for cross-border related-party transactions in an income year. Country-by-Country Reporting applies to New Zealand-headed multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of NZ$1.1 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate Gulf- or Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA 2007 s BG 1), CFC/FIF attribution rules, and the shareholder continuity and business continuity tests impose a de facto economic-substance requirement. A Tax_Exempt_Zone International Company must demonstrate genuine operational substance – real board control, decision-making, substantive books and records, and no central management and control exercised from New Zealand – otherwise the Commissioner may reclassify the entity as New Zealand-resident under s YD 2 and assess worldwide income at 28%, with shortfall penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating New Zealand-source OOG heavy-haul revenue on the IR4, inflating deductions attributable to foreign project legs, shifting profits into a tax-exempt International Company account, or destroying books and records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On conviction under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143A: fine up to NZ$50,000 for an individual and NZ$100,000 for a body corporate, and/or imprisonment up to five years. Civil shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall, plus use-of-money interest and full recovery of unpaid tax by distress and attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct false returns face personal criminal liability, restitution orders, travel bans pending prosecution, and civil veil-piercing to recover diverted project-cargo profits from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Offshore Shell / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a letter-box entity: no physical office, no employees, no board minutes, no substantive financial records, and central management and control exercised from New Zealand while still claiming Tax_Exempt_Zone status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may disregard the entity or arrangement under s BG 1 and s GA 1 ITA 2007, reassess all global profits at 28% as if the entity were New Zealand-resident, disallow loss offsets, impose shortfall penalties up to 100% (or 40% for an abusive tax position), and trigger deregistration under the Companies Act 1993.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused or knowingly facilitated the sham may be personally assessed under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 150 for unpaid PAYE and GST, subjected to travel bans, disqualified from directorship for up to ten years, or convicted for aiding tax evasion, with civil asset tracing and recovery against personal estates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing intercompany heavy-haul, craneage, route-escort or project-management services to a related offshore entity at zero margins or deliberately compressed markups in order to shift taxable profit from New Zealand OOG project-cargo contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue adjusts consideration to the arm's-length amount under s GC 7 ITA 2007, raising additional tax at 28%. Shortfall penalties of 20% (unacceptable tax position) up to 100% (evasion) may apply, together with use-of-money interest on underpaid tax. Deficient or non-existent transfer-pricing documentation triggers further documentation penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally engineered the pricing architecture are treated as parties to the avoidance arrangement and may be held personally liable for shortfall penalties where the company is insolvent; travel bans and restraint orders apply where evasion-level conduct is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach and Money Laundering Through Invoice-Led Remittance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting milestone wire transfers or letter-of-credit proceeds from undisclosed or opaque beneficial owners, processing payments through the tax-exempt International Company to launder criminal funds, or failing to apply customer due diligence and transaction monitoring for high-value OOG heavy-haul logistics payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: up to NZ$2,000,000 for a body corporate and NZ$200,000 for an individual per contravention. Criminal money-laundering conviction under Crimes Act 1961 s 243 carries imprisonment up to seven years and fines; asset forfeiture follows under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers face personal criminal exposure where they knew or were reckless about tainted funds, together with travel bans, asset freezing, civil recovery, director disqualification, and extradition risk in cross-border OOG logistics payment chains.
